hook_text: Two switches, four combinations, one sheet of paper. Write them all down and a gate can never surprise you again.
clip_script: A truth table lists every mix of inputs and the output each gives. Two inputs, four rows, counted in binary: 00, 01, 10, 11. AND: 0, 0, 0, 1, a single 1 at the bottom. OR: 0, 1, 1, 1, a single 0 at the top. They agree on both-off and both-on and differ only in the middle rows, where one switch is on; those are the rows that matter, the microwave door open with start pressed. Test every row on the bench, predicted against observed, tick, tick, tick, tick. Read it backwards: one 1 at the bottom, series switches; one 0 at the top, parallel.
visual_style: Whiteboard grid of four rows filling in; switches click through each row as a lamp lights or stays dark; two tables side by side with the middle rows highlighted; an arrow from a table to a switch circuit.
pacing: Table structure, AND fill and test, OR fill, comparison, reading back.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and test both tables on the bench, row by row.
